title: A Spartans Face?
description: In the beta release of Halo 3 multiplayer mode, if you angle the camera just right while on a mongoose, you can clip through the Spartan's helmet and it'll show a face underneath. Which is the image of Marcus Lehto, Bungie's creative director from 1997 to 2012.

title: Load Screen Message
description: Whilst your on the loading screen on December 25th (Christmas Day), if you press down on both thumbsticks a wider view of teh Halo Ring will display and if you look closely you can make out 'Happy Birthday, Lauren!' displayed on the rings surface.

title: Futuristic Aang
description: An original concept for Aang had him coming from a Futuristic Sci-Fi world, with Aang being the last suvivor taking him 1000 years into the future as the world reverts back to a more ancient time. Momo would also be a robot cyclops monkey which sounds pretty cool (not that we'd ever want to change him).

title: Kuroks Short Life
description: Avatar Kurok is the shortest living Avatar, he died at the age of 33. This was caused by Avatar Yangchen, who neglected the spirits, because of this every time Angry Spirits invaded the world. When Kurok defeated them some of his life energy would be drained eventually killing him.

title: Why Skyrim?
description: Skyrim was chosen as the next game in The Elder Scrolls series after Oblivion, was because the most was known about the province of Skyrim.It gave Bethesda more to start with as they developed the game. Along with the fact that Skyrim was considered cool

title: A Positive Attitude
description: Brian Fargo the co-creator of the Fallout series, went on record to confirm that the Vault Boy Thumbs-up depiction wasn't to see how close you are to atomic bomb blast (if it's bigger than your thumb you're in the radiation zone). Vault Boy simply has a 'Positive Attitude'

title: Experienced Thief
description: Stephen Russell the voice actor behind the leader of the Thieves Guild Mercer Frey in Skyrim, is also the voice actor for Garrett from the Thief Series, clearly Stephen is the ultimate Thief.

title: The Gnomeregan Punch Cards
description: Scattered throughout the Gnomeregan dungeon are collectible punch cards, each stamped with a string of binary code. Decode them and you'll find a set of silly, lore-flavoured in-jokes, including one that simply reads 'if you can read this, you're standing too close.'

title: A Lost Island in Sholazar Basin
description: Swim out into Bittertide Lake in Sholazar Basin and you'll find a tiny island with a hatch set into the ground. A plaque beside it reads a string of numbers that's a cheeky one-digit-higher twist on the famous recurring sequence from the TV show Lost.

title: Cryptids of the Deeprun Tram
description: The underwater stretch of the Deeprun Tram, which links Stormwind and Ironforge, occasionally has visitors: a Loch Ness-style sea serpent, a huge basking shark, the odd diver, and a chest that spawns and vanishes without explanation.

title: Karazhan's Hidden Smiley Face
description: Beneath the iconic wizard's tower of Karazhan, the developers hid a giant smiley face in the terrain. It's normally buried, but relogging near the tower or clipping through rubble at the right spot reveals it grinning back up at you.

title: Stratholme's Ghostly Dancers
description: Stratholme is the site of one of Warcraft's darkest moments, where Arthas Menethil purged the city's population. Some of the ghostly former citizens who still wander the ruins will respond if you use the /dance or /rude emotes on them.

title: The Sunken Gnome City
description: Far off the southeastern coast of Tanaris, past the point where fatigue starts to set in, lies the ruin of an abandoned gnomish settlement resting underwater. It's Azeroth's own little Atlantis, and its full story has never been told in-game.

title: The Goldshire Demon Children
description: Goldshire is one of the first towns Alliance players ever see, but around 6am server time it briefly turns sinister: six children spawn, walk in a tight pentagram formation, and head upstairs in a nearby house, with unsettling sound cues if you follow them.

title: A Genie Tribute to Robin Williams
description: Robin Williams was reportedly a keen Alliance player. After his death in 2014, Blizzard added a quiet tribute on an island off the southern coast of Talador: rub the Ever-Burning Lamp there and one of his most famous characters appears.

title: Florist Gump
description: In the Canal District of Stormwind runs a flower shop owned by a man named Bernard Gump, a florist with an unmistakable nod in his name to Tom Hanks' Forrest Gump. A second, older reference (a long-missing character called Gubber Blump) predates him.

title: Stormsong Valley's Harry Potter Tribute
description: In Stormsong Valley you can find NPCs named Severus the Outcast, Harald the Scarred, Ranald Flamehair, and Herme the Wise,  a playful stand-in for Severus Snape and the Harry Potter trio, part of a wider scattering of wizarding-world nods across the game.

title: Roscoe and Rachele: A Friends Tribute
description: In Dalaran's Legerdemain Lounge, a human named Roscoe and a blood elf named Rachele sit across from each other on the coffee shop's centre couches,  a clear stand-in for Ross and Rachel from Friends. Rachele will occasionally wonder aloud where 'Phoe'be' has got to.

title: The Corrupted Blood Incident
description: In September 2005, a debuff meant to stay contained to a single raid boss, Hakkar the Soulflayer, escaped into the wider world through infected pets. The resulting outbreak spread through capital cities so effectively that epidemiologists later studied it as a real model for how populations react to disease.

title: Harrison Jones, Azeroth's Indiana Jones
description: First appearing in Zul'Aman, this human archaeologist wears the trademark hat, carries a whip, and even complains about a fear of snakes and rats. He later became Stormwind's archaeology trainer and stars in one of Uldum's most memorable quest chains.

title: Zaalendor the Zoolander
description: Down on Ashran's Stormshield hub is an NPC named Zaalendor, who strikes three signature modelling poses,  Azure Steel, Le Talbuk, and Magnuum,  direct nods to Derek Zoolander's Blue Steel, Le Tigre, and Magnum.

title: The Westfall Chicken
description: Use the /chicken emote on a chicken enough times and it'll get fed up and offer you a quest, 'CLUCK!' Buy Special Chicken Feed from a nearby farmer, hand it over, and you're rewarded with a summonable chicken companion,  one of the game's oldest and strangest vanity pets.

title: Dormus the Camel-Hoarder
description: Camel figurines scattered across Uldum usually just crumble to dust when examined, but rarely one will teleport you to a hidden area called the Steam Pools. There you'll face a huge ettin, Dormus, who drops the Reins of the Grey Riding Camel mount and a matching title if defeated.

title: Sarah Kerrigan in the Shredder Cockpit
description: Peer into the cockpit of any Goblin Shredder and you'll spot a small image of Sarah Kerrigan, the Queen of Blades from StarCraft, glowing on the control panel. The Sky Golem mount, which shares the Shredder's design, updates the picture to her StarCraft II appearance.

title: The M-K Memorial
description: On a hill southwest of Crossroads in the Barrens sits a small shrine dedicated to an orc marked only with the initials 'M-K.' It honours Michel Koiter, a Blizzard illustrator who passed away during the game's development,  a spirit healer named Koiter can be found nearby.

title: Bambina and the Hunter
description: In Grizzly Hills you can find a young deer named Bambina wandering with a rabbit (Thudder) and a skunk (Flora),  a clear Bambi reference. Wait around and a scripted hunter appears to shoot Bambina's mother, sending the fawn into a berserk, 2,000%-damage rage.

title: Xur'ios, Destiny's Vendor in Disguise
description: Tucked near Dalaran's Antonidas Memorial is an ethereal vendor called Xur'ios, who deals exclusively in Curious Coins. It's a direct homage to Destiny's Xur, right down to selling items named after that game's gear, like 'Gjallar's Horn' and 'Krota's Shield.'

title: The Original Loot Cave
description: Shortly after launch in 2014, players discovered a cave in the Skywatch area of the Cosmodrome where low-level enemies respawned almost instantly. Guardians lined up to farm it for easy Engrams and XP, turning it into one of the most infamous grinding spots in gaming history before Bungie patched it out.

title: The Loot Cave's Haunted Message
description: After the loot cave was patched, Bungie left behind a pile of charred Hive Thrall corpses at the site. Interacting with the remains triggers a distorted voice line about a million deaths not being enough for Master Rahool, a cheeky nod to how many enemies were farmed there for Cryptarch decoding.

title: A Possible Dune Reference
description: The haunted loot cave voice line bears a striking resemblance to a line from Frank Herbert's novel Dune about deaths not being enough for a character named Yueh. Bungie has never confirmed whether the similarity was an intentional literary nod or coincidence.

title: Grasp of Avarice Was Built Around the Loot Cave
description: Years after Destiny 1 ended, Bungie revisited the Cosmodrome loot cave as the setting for the Grasp of Avarice dungeon in Destiny 2's 30th Anniversary Pack, spinning the community's favourite exploit into an in-universe story about a fireteam corrupted by greed.

title: The Alpha Line That Got Cut
description: During Destiny's public alpha, Ghost's flat delivery of a line about a wizard coming from the Moon was mocked so heavily online that Bungie pulled it from the final game entirely, an early sign the Ghost's dialogue and performance would become a lasting point of community ridicule.

title: Peter Dinklage's 'Dinklebot'
description: Ghost was originally voiced by Game of Thrones star Peter Dinklage, whose flat, monotone delivery became so widely mocked that fans nicknamed the character 'Dinklebot.' The nickname spread quickly online even during the alpha test, before the full game had released.

title: Ghost Got a Complete Voice Recast
description: For The Taken King expansion, Bungie replaced Dinklage with veteran voice actor Nolan North, best known for Nathan Drake in Uncharted. Remarkably, North didn't just voice new lines, he re-recorded every single piece of Ghost dialogue from the original base game so the whole experience would feel consistent.

title: McCartney's Shelved Musical Suite
description: 'Hope for the Future' was originally part of a larger orchestral suite McCartney composed for Destiny called 'Music of the Spheres.' Bungie shelved the full suite during development, and it wasn't released to the public until 2018, bundled with vinyl preorders of a Destiny soundtrack collection.

title: Xur's Design Echoes Resident Evil's Merchant
description: The weekend exotic vendor Xur, hooded coat, backpack, and unsettling stare, bears a strong visual resemblance to the mysterious Merchant from Resident Evil 4. His tentacled face has also been noted by fans as a nod to Lovecraft's Cthulhu Mythos.

title: Why Xur Stands Hunched
description: In later lore, the Guardian Orin confronts Xur while investigating the Nine, crushing his throat and striking him with a war hammer hard enough to warp his spine permanently. It's why Xur has always stood in that distinctive hunched posture and spoken in his strained voice.

title: Xur Almost Missed Its Big Debut
description: The legendary exotic rocket launcher Gjallarhorn was sold by Xur only three times across the game's entire history, twice in Destiny 1's first year. Many players missed or ignored the very first sale simply because they didn't yet realise how good it was or didn't have enough Strange Coins.

title: Ghosts Might Predate the Traveler's Arrival
description: One piece of Destiny promotional material implied Ghosts already existed during humanity's Golden Age, which contradicts nearly every other in-game source stating the Traveler created Ghosts only after the Collapse. Fans generally treat it as an oversight rather than confirmed lore.

title: Dead Ghosts Hide Grimoire Lore Everywhere
description: Scattered across every world in the original Destiny are broken, inactive Ghosts that glow faintly blue. Reviving one unlocks a hidden Grimoire lore card, and hunting down fifty of them was rewarded with the 'Ghost Hunter' achievement.

title: Your Ship Actually Lands in the Tower
description: The ships buzzing around Tower Plaza aren't just decorative background traffic. If you sprint into the Tower Hangar the instant you spawn in, you can actually catch your own Guardian's ship being flown in and lowered into the hangar below.

title: Destiny's First Easter Egg Predates the Game
description: Years before Destiny released, an advertising billboard reading 'Destiny Awaits' appeared in Bungie's Halo 3: ODST, complete with an image of Earth and what looks like the Traveler hovering above it, an early, subtle tease of the studio's next project.

title: Players Found a Hidden Zone Beyond the Black Garden
description: About a week after Destiny's launch, players discovered a large, empty, otherwise inaccessible map area reachable only by exploiting the Black Garden location, one of the first big community-driven secret discoveries in the game.

title: Vault of Glass's Secret Chest
description: Tucked into the raid's Gorgon's Labyrinth section is a hidden chest reachable only after a chasm jump across disappearing platforms, sitting just off the main path right before the corridor leading to Atheon's chamber.

title: Cosmetic Coins Hidden in Plain Sight
description: Scattered around the Tower and other social spaces are small, non-interactive coins visually identical to the collectible Destiny Coin. They can be spotted tucked into bushes, tree branches, and rafters, but can never actually be picked up.

title: Xur Once Bugged Out of Selling a Key Item
description: During Rise of Iron, a code bug caused Xur to stop offering Three of Coins, a consumable many players relied on to boost exotic drop chances, for several consecutive weekends before Bungie caught and fixed the issue.

title: Nolan North's Uncanny Cayde-6 Impression
description: After Nolan North took over as Ghost, he later also voiced Cayde-6 following Nathan Fillion's departure from the role, recording an entire set of cutscenes, including Cayde's own death scene, in a near-flawless impression of Fillion's original performance.

title: The Nine Remain Deliberately Unexplained
description: Xur repeatedly tells Guardians that his will belongs to the Nine and that he can't fully explain their purpose. A Grimoire card in the original game lays out several competing, unconfirmed theories about who or what the Nine actually are, leaving their true nature intentionally ambiguous.

title: Bungie's Cameo on the Ark
description: Deep in the campaign level The Ark, near the seventh data terminal, players can find a floating cardboard cutout of Bungie co-founder Jason Jones, dressed in nothing but a pair of gym shorts. It's one of several in-jokes the studio hid throughout the level for eagle-eyed fans who go looking off the beaten path.

title: Bungie Will Never Confirm Them All
description: Bungie deliberately kept the full scope of Halo 3's secrets a mystery even after launch. When fans asked the community team directly whether every easter egg had been found, the response was blunt: players would never find them all, and Bungie wouldn't be giving out hints, because the mystery was part of the magic.

title: The Vidmaster Road to Recon
description: For years, the coveted Recon Armour wasn't something you could simply unlock in-game. Getting it meant completing a brutal set of Vidmaster Challenges spread across Halo 3 and Halo 3: ODST, things like finishing a level solo on Legendary without ever firing a shot or throwing a grenade. Complete them all and Bungie would grant you the Armour through their 'Road to Recon' program on Bungie.net.

title: Challenges That Didn't Ship at Launch
description: The Vidmaster Challenges weren't actually part of Halo 3 when it launched in September 2007. They were added almost a year later through a title update released in September 2008, meaning the toughest achievements in the game were a post-launch surprise for the community rather than a day-one feature.

title: Recon Armour for Everyone
description: The exclusivity didn't last forever. As Bungie handed the reins of the franchise to 343 Industries, the studio gave every Halo 3 player the Recon Armour permutation for free on March 29, 2012, closing the book on one of the game's most difficult unlocks.

title: Skulls You Could Only Find in Forge
description: Alongside the classic campaign skulls, Bungie hid a separate set of skulls exclusively inside Forge-enabled multiplayer maps like Sandbox, Assembly, and Orbital, later expanding the hunt with three more skulls on maps added by Halo 3: ODST. These didn't unlock cheats like the campaign skulls did, but collecting all of them triggered its own dedicated achievement.

title: 800,000 Players Beta Tested the Multiplayer
description: Months before release, Bungie opened a public multiplayer beta to anyone who bought Crackdown. It wasn't just a marketing gimmick,  in the space of three weeks the beta pulled in more than 800,000 unique players, effectively turning early access into one of the biggest live playtests in gaming history up to that point.

title: The Biggest Entertainment Launch of Its Time
description: When Halo 3 launched on September 25, 2007, it didn't just break gaming records,  it outsold the opening weekends of major Hollywood films. Reports at the time put day-one earnings north of $170 million, with roughly 3.3 million copies sold in the first week alone, edging past openings like Spider-Man 3 and the release of the final Harry Potter novel.

title: A War Memorial Built to Sell a Game
description: Rather than lean on gameplay footage, Halo 3's centerpiece 'Believe' campaign built a physical diorama over 1,200 square feet in size, a miniature war memorial populated with hundreds of hand-sculpted human and Covenant figures at one-twelfth scale. Fans could pan across the entire model on a dedicated website, and the ad series went on to win gold at Cannes Lions the following year.

title: An Alternate Reality Game Hidden in the Forums
description: Halo 3's viral marketing kicked off in a strange way: on June 11, 2007, Bungie.net's forums appeared to be 'hacked,' setting off months of clue-hunting as fans pieced together hidden servers that gradually revealed the final days of the Forerunners. The campaign, known as Iris, folded story lore directly into the game's real-world promotion.

title: Why It's Called the Gravemind
description: The name of the Flood's central intelligence wasn't lifted from any existing mythology,  it was coined by Bungie staff writer Jaime Griesemer specifically for the character. The Gravemind is voiced throughout the trilogy by actor Dee Bradley Baker, known for his extensive voice work across animation and games.

title: A Poet Older Than Your God
description: The Gravemind almost always speaks in a distinct poetic meter, trochaic heptameter, and when Cortana challenges it on this habit, it explains that it carries the memories of countless poets from cultures far beyond human experience, giving it both the vocabulary and the quickness of mind to compose verse as it speaks rather than labour over words.

title: The Gravemind Betrays Everyone, Every Time
description: At the Ark, the Gravemind strikes an uneasy truce with both Master Chief and the Arbiter, helping them cut down the Prophet of Truth and even manipulating Truth's own infection to seal his fate. The moment the shared goal is achieved, though, the Gravemind turns on its erstwhile allies immediately, forcing the two to fight their way clear before it can finish what it started.

title: Master Chief's Given Name
description: Behind the Spartan number and the legendary Armour, Master Chief has a first name that rarely comes up in dialogue: John. The Gravemind is one of the very few beings in the wider universe ever shown learning and using it, a small but telling detail about how much the Flood's intelligence comes to know about the humans it hunts.

title: Cortana's Distorted Interludes
description: Throughout the campaign, Cortana and the Gravemind periodically break into the Chief's mind through what Bungie internally called 'character interludes.' During these moments the screen washes with color, background music cuts out, and player movement slows drastically, a deliberate way of weaving story beats directly into gameplay rather than pulling players out to a cutscene.

title: A Trapped Marine Loses His Mind
description: The Gravemind's telepathic voice isn't only heard by the Chief. According to the wider lore, a Marine once overheard it speaking through nearby combat forms and was driven to insanity by what's known as the logic plague, implied to have taken his own life off-screen as a result. It's a small aside that hints at just how psychologically dangerous simply being near the Flood's collective mind can be.

title: Morse Code on High Ground
description: Tucked inside the defensive base on the multiplayer map High Ground is a small machine that quietly taps out a message in Morse code. It was spotted as far back as the Halo 3 multiplayer beta, and the elevator music playing in the same room hides its own layer of secrecy for anyone patient enough to sit and listen.

title: Carvings in the First Level's Trees
description: Right from the opening level, Sierra 117, Bungie hid a string of small carvings in the jungle's tree trunks, from an initialed love note and a date to a tiny caveman figure and even a whole hidden caveman family. They're easy to run straight past, but they were part of a much longer campaign-wide easter egg hunt players pieced together over the years.

title: A Computer Screen Straight Out of Windows
description: Inside the Sandtrap multiplayer map's temple, where the giant Elephant vehicle is parked, sits a two-screen laptop that will occasionally flash up a fake Windows-style error screen, complete with the kind of garbled system text you'd expect from a crashed PC rather than a 26th-century UNSC terminal.

title: One Billion Matches and Counting
description: Halo 3's multiplayer wasn't just a launch-week phenomenon. By March 2009, more than one billion online matches had been played across the game, and it had gone on to sell over 14.5 million copies in total, making it one of the best-selling titles of its console generation.

title: Forge Mode Makes Its Debut
description: Halo 3 introduced Forge, an in-game object editor that let players reshape multiplayer maps by moving, adding, or removing pieces of scenery and weapons. It was far more limited than a full PC map editor, but it laid the groundwork for the custom map culture that would define Halo's multiplayer community for years afterward.

title: The Mount Chiliad Mural
description: Inside the cable car lift station at the top of Mount Chiliad, players can find a strange painted mural showing a UFO, a cracking egg, and a figure using a jetpack. The mural fuelled one of gaming's longest-running community investigations, spawning an entire subreddit dedicated to decoding it.

title: Golden Peyote and the Sasquatch
description: A hidden 'Golden Peyote' plant lets players transform into Bigfoot, but it only appears at Raton Canyon on Tuesdays between 5:30 and 8:00 AM, and only once every prior peyote plant has already been consumed. It was one of the last major single-player secrets fans uncovered after release.

title: Bigfoot on the City Seal
description: Look closely at the official seal of the City of Los Santos, which appears on the side of every LSPD patrol vehicle, and you'll spot a small illustration of Bigfoot tucked into the bottom right corner, a quiet nod to the series' long-running cryptid mythology.

title: Franklin's Nine-Year Hunt
description: In the Strangers and Freaks mission 'The Last One', Franklin meets a hunter who claims he's been chasing a Sasquatch for nine years. That's a deliberate reference to GTA: San Andreas, released exactly nine years before GTA V, where rumours of a Bigfoot sighting first took hold of the community.

title: Rockstar's Tuesday Taunt
description: When data-miners first located the coordinates for the game's hidden Golden Peyote, they found a comment left directly in GTA V's source code by Rockstar, ribbing the discoverer for starting the hunt on the wrong day of the week: 'he was wrong to start his hunt on Tuesday.'

title: The Most Expensive Game Ever Made
description: GTA V's development cost is estimated at around $265 million, with a further $128-150 million spent on marketing, bringing the total to roughly $400 million. At the time of its 2013 launch, that made it the single most expensive entertainment product ever produced.

title: Three Protagonists, One Story
description: GTA V was the first game in the series to let players simultaneously control three separate protagonists: Michael, Franklin, and Trevor. Each character required their own voice recording, motion capture sessions, animations, and dedicated mission strands, a huge driver of the game's production cost.

title: A Billion Dollars in Three Days
description: GTA V recouped its enormous budget almost instantly, generating more than $1 billion in revenue within just three days of launch and setting multiple entertainment industry sales records in the process.

title: Master Chief Busking in Vinewood
description: Wander through Vinewood's 'Chinatown' district and you can find street performers dressed as identical copies of Halo's Master Chief, posing for tips just like the costumed performers found on real Hollywood Boulevard.

title: Drive's Jacket, Reimagined
description: A clothing shop near Trevor's rink in Sandy Shores sells a whitish jacket with a crab stitched onto the back, a direct parody of the iconic scorpion jacket Ryan Gosling's character wears throughout the 2011 film Drive.

title: The Gone in 60 Seconds Garage
description: During the campaign, players can enter a garage containing a list of cars that's only visible under ultraviolet light, a clear homage to the target vehicle list from the heist film Gone in 60 Seconds.

title: Claptrap on the Construction Site
description: Several pieces of construction machinery scattered around Los Santos are decorated with designs and paint jobs that closely resemble Claptrap, the excitable robot companion from the Borderlands series.

title: Floyd's Jackie Brown Apartment
description: Floyd's apartment, which Trevor breaks into during the story, is laid out almost identically to Melanie's apartment from Quentin Tarantino's 1997 film Jackie Brown, right down to the furniture arrangement.

title: Maibatsu's Roots in GTA 2
description: The in-game Maibatsu Corporation's name is a knowing echo of 'Zaibatsu', the fictional business conglomerate that dominated Grand Theft Auto 2, one of many self-referential threads Rockstar weaves back through its own series history.

title: Los Santos' Playboy Mansion
description: Tucked into the Richman district is a mansion lit up with pink lights, a wraparound driveway, and elaborate landscaping, an unmistakable replica of the real-world Playboy Mansion. Visit at night and you'll find a party in full swing out by the pool.

title: Fifty-Plus Hidden Secrets
description: According to GameSpot's own dedicated hunt for the game's secrets, GTA V's map hides more than 50 documented easter eggs, ranging from tiny visual gags to fully triggerable side quests.

title: The Sunken Submarine Fortune
description: One of the largest single cash stashes in the game, $25,000, sits on top of a wrecked submarine deep underwater, next to the vessel's entrance hatch, rewarding players willing to dive for it.

title: The Infinite 8 Killer's Trail
description: Scattered clues hidden throughout Los Santos and Blaine County let players follow the trail of a fictional serial killer known as the Infinite 8 Killer, eventually leading to the discovery of his victims' bodies.

title: GTA Online's Legendary Parents
description: In the GTA Online character creator, players can choose Claude from GTA III, Niko Bellic from GTA IV, or John Marston from Red Dead Redemption as their custom protagonist's father, quietly tying the online world into the wider Rockstar universe.

title: The Ghost of Mount Gordo
description: Between 11:00 PM and midnight, a stationary female ghost appears on the eastern peak of Mount Gordo. She won't move or react to being shot at, and simply fades away, one of several ghostly sightings Rockstar seeded into the world.

title: A Twelve-Year Community Obsession
description: The Mount Chiliad mural spawned an entire dedicated subreddit, r/ChiliadMystery, where fans spent over a decade cross-referencing glyphs, murals, and in-game code in the hope of uncovering a hidden reward, becoming one of gaming's longest-running amateur investigations.

title: A Thousand-Strong Development Team
description: GTA V's development team swelled to more than 1,000 people at its peak, with production spanning over five years and some staff reportedly logging over 100-hour work weeks to hit the game's original release window.

title: The Giant Squid in the Assassin Tomb
description: Inside the Assassin Tomb beneath Santa Maria della Visitazione, if Ezio stares into the water near the first lever for about a minute, a cutscene plays showing a giant squid swimming past. Look again and a tentacle nearly slaps him.

title: "It's-a-me, Mario!"
description: When Ezio first meets his uncle Mario Auditore, Mario greets him with "It's-a-me! Mario!",  a direct lift of the first line spoken by Mario in Super Mario 64.

title: Another Capering Crusader
description: While free-running or climbing, a male bystander occasionally mutters "Another capering crusader," a nod to Batman, who is nicknamed the Caped Crusader and shares Ezio's love of rooftops and stealth.

title: Ghosts of the Auditore Family
description: After meeting Niccolò Machiavelli, returning to the Palazzo Auditore courtyard and using Eagle Vision triggers a one-time-only vision of Ezio's entire deceased family standing around the palazzo.

title: Keys That Go Nowhere
description: Looting practice dummies during the missions "Knowledge Is Power" and "Hunting the Hunter" grants the player keys, leftover, dummied-out content that serves absolutely no purpose in the game.

title: "Money! That's What I Want!"
description: Throw coins into a crowd and female bystanders will sometimes shout "Money! That's what I want!", a reference to the Motown classic of the same name.

title: Carlo's Cowering Confession
description: If every guard in the Doge's Palace is pre-assassinated before confronting Carlo Grimaldi, he flees to the bottom of the Giants' Staircase and cowers, lip-syncing dialogue lifted straight from the game's original E3 demo.

title: The Crashed Glider
description: After assassinating Carlo Grimaldi, heading to the Venice dock area lets players find Da Vinci's flying machine still lying wrecked where it crashed earlier in the story.

title: The Doge's Frozen Chessboard
description: Glitching into the Palazzo Ducale's private quarters reveals the exact chess position from the cutscene where Carlo Grimaldi assassinated Doge Giovanni Mocenigo, though the candle they played under is oddly unlit, and the sky outside turns blood red, likely an unintended lighting bug.

title: Subject 16's Twenty Glyphs
description: Subject 16 hid twenty encoded Glyphs across the Animus recreation of Renaissance Italy, five in Florence, one in Monteriggioni, five in Tuscany, two in Romagna, and seven in Venice,  each unlocking a fragment of the video known as "The Truth."

title: Adam, Eve, and the Binary for Eden
description: Assembling all twenty Glyphs unlocks "The Truth," a short video depicting a man and woman named Adam and Eve running through a futuristic setting called Eden. The video closes on a binary string that translates directly to the word EDEN.

title: The Apple-Hidden Paintings Puzzle
description: One Glyph puzzle asks players to find the shared element across five famous paintings, including Atalanta and Hippomenes and The Fall, the answer being that each artwork secretly depicts an Apple of Eden.

title: The Hopi Prophecy Hidden in a Glyph
description: Solving a sonar-based Glyph puzzle reveals a hidden message quoting a Hopi prophecy warning of "a container of ashes" thrown from the sky that would burn the land and boil the ocean, an omen tying into the series' looming solar-flare apocalypse.

title: "Nothing Is True, Everything Is Permitted"
description: One of the Glyph puzzles displays the Assassin creed itself, "Nothing is True, Everything is Permitted," and is deliberately unsolvable in the traditional sense,  there is no right or wrong answer, only the phrase itself.

title: Ezio's Real Family Feud: The Sforza Assassination
description: Although he never appears on screen, the real-life assassination of Galeazzo Maria Sforza, Duke of Milan, is referenced in letters Giovanni Auditore writes to Lorenzo de' Medici, framing it as the opening spark of the game's Templar conspiracy in 1476.

title: Caterina Sforza Was Galeazzo's Daughter
description: Caterina Sforza, one of the game's major allies and a romantic interest for Ezio, was the real illegitimate daughter of Galeazzo Maria Sforza,  the same Duke of Milan whose assassination kicks off the story.

title: Machiavelli Was a Real Political Philosopher
description: Niccolò Machiavelli, Ezio's mentor figure in the Italian Brotherhood, was a genuine Renaissance diplomat and writer widely regarded as the father of modern political science.

title: Da Vinci Really Moved to Milan, Not Venice
description: In-game, Leonardo da Vinci relocates his workshop from Florence to Venice in 1481. In real history, Leonardo left Florence for Milan that year, not Venice,  a deliberate artistic liberty so Ezio's ally could stay close during the Venice chapters.

title: Da Vinci's Inventions Were Never Actually Built
description: The flying machine and tank Ezio uses in-game were real Leonardo da Vinci designs, but neither was ever constructed in his lifetime,  he reportedly worried about his blueprints falling into the wrong hands and included deliberate errors in his notes.

title: "Virtù" and The Prince
description: When Machiavelli asks how Ezio recruited the city's guilds, Ezio credits "Virtù," a real concept from Machiavelli's writing on leadership. Later, Machiavelli jokes about writing a book on Ezio one day,  a wink at Machiavelli's real, famously short work, The Prince.

title: The Sistine Chapel's Missing Ceiling
description: Visit the Sistine Chapel in-game and Michelangelo's famous ceiling fresco is nowhere to be seen, not a graphical shortcut, but historical accuracy, since the game is set in 1499, several years before Michelangelo began that work.

title: Desmond's Red Footprints
description: Standing outside the Villa Auditore as Desmond and activating Eagle Vision reveals a trail of red footprints leading to the Assassin insignia, an unused navigational aid the developers later admitted was an oversight, since red was meant to signal danger, not direction.

title: The Empire Strikes Back Hidden in a Frozen Cave
entertainment: Star Wars: Episode V - The Empire Strikes Back
description: Deep in Bleakcoast Cave, southeast of Winterhold, players who clear out the resident frost trolls will find a skeleton suspended upside down in the ceiling ice with a sword lying just out of reach below it. It's a direct recreation of Luke Skywalker's capture by the Wampa on Hoth at the start of The Empire Strikes Back, right down to the frost trolls standing in for the Wampa.

title: A Pac-Man Made Entirely of Cheese
description: Inside Endon's house in Markarth, a wheel of cheese has been carved into a perfect Pac-Man shape, complete with a row of garlic cloves standing in for the dots he'd normally be chomping through in the arcade classic.

title: Excalibur and the Lady in the Lake
description: Near Bleakwind Basin, a skeletal arm reaches up out of a small lake clutching a sword, a nod to the Lady of the Lake handing Excalibur to King Arthur. A second sword-in-stone reference can also be found elsewhere in the game, both playing on the same legend.

title: Skyrim's Own Headless Horseman
description: A rare wandering NPC known as the Headless Horseman roams Skyrim's roads at night, a reference to Washington Irving's The Legend of Sleepy Hollow. He's easy to miss since most players fast-travel rather than ride the roads, but following him leads to a decent reward.

title: A Whole Quest Built on The Hangover
description: The Daedric quest 'A Night to Remember' has the Dragonborn wake up after a blackout night with the Daedric Prince Sanguine, then retrace their steps across Skyrim to fix the chaos they caused, mirroring the plot of the 2009 comedy The Hangover beat for beat.

title: 'My Precious' from a Hagraven
description: During 'A Night to Remember', a hagraven named Moira mutters 'my precious' while trying to hold onto a wedding ring the player needs, a direct callback to Gollum's obsession with the One Ring in The Lord of the Rings.

title: A Frozen Recreation of 300
description: South of the Shrine to Peryite, a skeleton is found wedged in a narrow mountain pass with a saber cat impaled on a glass sword beside it, restaging the scene from 300 where Leonidas traps and kills a wolf in a narrow pass using a similar technique.

title: Alduin's Wall Charts the Entire Series
description: The massive stone carving known as Alduin's Wall, which kicks off the hunt for the Dragonrend shout, hides visual references to events from earlier Elder Scrolls games: the Staff of Chaos from Arena, Numidium from Daggerfall, Red Mountain from Morrowind, and an Oblivion Gate from Oblivion, all worked into the carved history of the World-Eater.

title: The East Empire Company Is the East India Company
description: The East Empire Company, a recurring monopolistic trading operation in the series since Morrowind's Bloodmoon expansion, is a deliberate stand-in for the real-world East India Company. Its Skyrim warehouse even hides various in-game drugs, echoing the East India Company's real history of smuggling.

title: The Statues of Sovngarde Turn to Watch You
description: The giant statues found in Sovngarde, the Nordic realm of the honored dead, will quietly rotate to face the player whenever they aren't being watched directly, a subtle detail that most players never catch happening in real time.

title: The Sweetroll Joke Predates Skyrim by 17 Years
description: Skyrim guards mocking the player with 'let me guess, someone stole your sweetroll' is the punchline to a much older running gag. The sweetroll first appeared as a character-creation question in 1994's The Elder Scrolls: Arena, resurfaced in Daggerfall and Morrowind, and was even asked by Emperor Uriel Septim in Oblivion's tutorial moments before his assassination.

title: Darth Vader's Helmet in Ysgramor's Tomb
description: Hidden inside Ysgramor's Tomb, only accessible during a Companions questline, sits a helmet modeled after Darth Vader's iconic mask, one of two direct Star Wars references built into Skyrim.

title: Dragon Priests Were Once Living Rulers of Skyrim
description: Before becoming the undead lich-like bosses players fight in ancient tombs, the Dragon Priests were living members of the Dragon Cult who ruled over Nord society on behalf of the dragons during the Merethic Era, wielding power and knowledge granted directly by their draconic masters.

title: Alduin Isn't Meant to Be Purely Evil
description: Alduin, the 'World-Eater' players fight throughout Skyrim's main quest, is a child of Akatosh, the God of Time, whose true purpose is to eventually devour the world so a new one can begin. His war against humanity stems from pride and a refusal to accept that duty rather than pure malice, and after his defeat, Arngeir suggests he may one day return to fulfil it.

title: Miraak Was the First Dragonborn, and He Betrayed the Dragons
description: Long before the Dragonborn of Skyrim, Miraak served as a Dragon Priest who was seduced by the Daedric Prince Hermaeus Mora with promises of forbidden knowledge and power. He began conspiring against his own dragon overlords, a betrayal explored fully in the Dragonborn expansion.

title: The Dark Brotherhood's Night Mother Was Once Just a Grieving Mother
description: According to Dark Brotherhood lore, the Night Mother began as a nameless woman with five children who was approached by the Daedric Prince Sithis and offered a place at his side in exchange for killing her own children. She accepted, murdered them, and became the undead matron figure the Dark Brotherhood still worships in Skyrim.

title: M'aiq the Liar Has Wandered Every Elder Scrolls Game Since Morrowind
description: M'aiq the Liar is a wandering Khajiit who appears somewhere in Skyrim, dispensing cryptic, often fourth-wall-breaking commentary on the game itself. He's a recurring series in-joke, having also turned up in Morrowind and Oblivion, always deliberately unreliable about what he tells the player.

title: Skyrim Launched on 11/11/11 for a Reason
description: Bethesda deliberately released Skyrim worldwide on November 11, 2011, exactly a year after announcing it at the 2010 Spike Video Game Awards on November 11, 2010, turning the memorable 11/11/11 date into part of the game's marketing and cultural identity.

title: One In-Game Book Lets You Choose Your Own Adventure
description: The in-game book 'Kolb and the Dragon' functions as a playable choose-your-own-adventure story within Skyrim itself, letting the reader pick different paths through the narrative rather than simply reading static text like the game's other books.

title: There Are Thirteen Named Dragon Priests in Total
description: The base game features eight named Dragon Priest bosses, each guarding a unique enchanted mask with its own powerful effect. The Dragonborn expansion adds five more named Dragon Priests, bringing the total to thirteen, four of which carry their own unique masks.

title: Summoning a Hidden Dragon in Blackreach
description: A dragon named Vulthuryol can be found sealed within the underground region of Blackreach. Players can summon it by using the Unrelenting Force shout on a glowing orb near the Debate Hall, triggering a rare underground dragon fight most players never intentionally seek out.

title: A Ghost Bard Can Boost Your Speech Skill
description: At Bard's Leap Summit, a ghostly bard named Azzadal appears and can grant the player a boost to their Speech skill, a small hidden reward tucked away at a location most players only visit for the scenic cliffside view.

title: Harold the Talking Tree
description: Deep in Oasis, at the northern edge of the map, you'll find Harold, a ghoul who has literally become one with a tree, now known as Bob. Harold first appeared as a mutated ghoul in the original two Fallout games, and his transformation into a sentient tree is one of the series' longest-running character arcs.

title: HAL 9000 Surveillance Cameras
description: Scattered around the Capital Wasteland are surveillance cameras with a distinctive red-eyed circular design, deliberately styled after HAL 9000, the malevolent AI from Stanley Kubrick's 2001: A Space Odyssey.

title: Crashed UFO and Alien Blaster
description: North of the MDPL-13 Power Station lies a crashed alien spacecraft with a dead extraterrestrial pilot still inside. Loot the wreckage and you'll find the Alien Blaster, one of the rarest and strangest weapons in the game.

title: The Lovecraft Library
description: In the far southwest of the map, south of Girdershade, sits a building stuffed with H.P. Lovecraft's writings and eerie cosmic-horror imagery, a quiet tribute tucked away from the game's main questlines.

title: USS Ozymandias and the Shelley Reference
description: The wrecked survey ship USS Ozymandias off the coast of Point Lookout is more than a scavenging spot. Its name, the quest 'An Antique Land,' and the in-game Bysshe Company are all references to Percy Bysshe Shelley's poem 'Ozymandias', right down to using the poet's own middle name.

title: "Burn That Goddamn Jumpsuit"
description: In Paradise Falls, a Vault 77 jumpsuit sits beside a holodisk sarcastically demanding it be burned. It's a direct callback to a Penny Arcade Fallout tie-in comic, one of the more obscure crossover nods Bethesda buried in the game.

title: The Shrinking Chess Set
description: Find a miniature chess board somewhere in the Wasteland and you'll be able to pick up tiny Nuka-Cola bottles, bears, and gnomes. Carry only one at a time and they'll stay miniature-sized in your inventory, a strange little physics quirk players still swap tips about.

title: Butch and the Stolen Sweetroll
description: During the Vault 101 birthday sequence, Butch DeLoria tries to snatch the sweetroll Old Lady Palmer just gave you. It's Bethesda's own running gag, echoing a famous line from the Elder Scrolls series about stolen sweetrolls.

title: "A Nice Day for a Right Wedding"
description: The quest title is a wasteland twist on Billy Idol's lyric 'it's a nice day for a white wedding', a small pun that only lands if you know the song.

title: Fawkes' Blade Runner Battle Cry
description: When Fawkes lands a power attack, he snarls 'Wake up... time to die!', a direct lift from Leon's line to Deckard in Blade Runner.

title: Rory McLaren's Cool Hand Luke Line
description: Rory McLaren will exclaim 'Nobody can eat 50 eggs!', a nod to the famous egg-eating bet at the heart of the 1967 Paul Newman film Cool Hand Luke.

title: Bryan Wilks and the TV Dinner Line
description: During the 'Those!' quest, young Bryan Wilks hides in a Pulowski Preservation shelter and mutters 'Now I know what a TV dinner feels like', a quote lifted straight from Die Hard.

title: Callahan's Magnum
description: The unique revolver Callahan's Magnum takes its name directly from Harry Callahan, Clint Eastwood's iconic character in Dirty Harry.

title: The McClellan Family Townhome's Bradbury Tribute
entertainment: There Will Come Soft Rains (Ray Bradbury)
description: This whole location is a deep-cut homage to Ray Bradbury. The self-operating house, the dead family dog outside, and the Mister Handy reciting a 1920s poem all mirror Bradbury's short story 'There Will Come Soft Rains.' The family surname is even a play on Bradbury's own name from Fahrenheit 451, and the house number references the story's setting year.

title: Sergeant RL-3's MacArthur Quote
description: The robotic companion Sergeant RL-3 declares 'Old warbots never die! We just rust away,' twisting General Douglas MacArthur's real-life farewell line, 'old soldiers never die; they just fade away.'

title: Mister Gutsy's Apocalypse Now Line
description: In combat, Mister Gutsy robots sometimes chirp 'there is nothing I like better than the smell of plasma in the morning', a rewrite of Robert Duvall's iconic napalm line from Apocalypse Now.

title: Charon's Beatles Reference
description: Ask ghoul companion Charon to switch to ranged weapons and he'll remark that he 'finds happiness in a warm gun', a nod to The Beatles' 'Happiness Is a Warm Gun.'

title: Robobrain's Portal Homage
description: When a Robobrain loses track of you, it may ask 'Are you still there?' Developer script notes explicitly label this line as an homage to Portal.

title: "You Can't Stop the Signal"
description: After completing the Galaxy News Radio quest, DJ Three Dog shouts 'You can't stop the signal!', a direct quote from the film Serenity.

title: The Bombs Fell on October 23, 2077
description: Within Fallout lore, the Great War's nuclear bombs fell on October 23, 2077. Bethesda actually wanted Fallout 3's real-world release date to land on that same date, but the game ended up hitting shelves a week later in North America instead.

title: The Adamantium Skeleton Perk
description: The Adamantium Skeleton perk borrows its name straight from Marvel's X-Men, referencing the fictional indestructible metal alloy bonded to Wolverine's bones.

title: Fallout 3 Was Announced Before Oblivion
description: Development on Fallout 3 quietly began in 2004, and the game was actually revealed to the public before Oblivion, which released two years earlier. Full production reportedly didn't ramp up until after Oblivion shipped.

title: The First Piece of Fallout 3 Art
description: The very first piece of concept art created for Fallout 3 was drawn by lead artist Istvan Pely back in 2004, an image of a lone figure in power armor that would go on to become the game's iconic box art.

title: V.A.T.S. Was Inspired by Burnout
description: The Vault-Tec Assisted Targeting System, V.A.T.S., reportedly took its slow-motion, cinematic inspiration from the Crash Mode replays in the racing game Burnout, just swapping crumpled cars for dismembered limbs.

title: Bill Clinton Was Considered for President Eden
description: According to the casting company involved, former U.S. President Bill Clinton was seriously considered, and even approached, to voice President John Henry Eden before Malcolm McDowell ultimately took the role.

title: The Pip-Boy's Awkward Control Layout
description: The Pip-Boy's artists later admitted a design regret: all the knobs and switches sit on the left side of the screen, despite the device being strapped to the left wrist and operated with the right hand, meaning your own hand blocks the display while adjusting it. Fallout 4 fixed this by moving the controls to the right side.

title: The Fat Man's Cut RC Plane
description: Early in development, the mini-nuke launcher known as the Fat Man was designed to carry its warhead on a remote-controlled model B-17 bomber rather than firing it as a simple projectile, a concept that never made it to the final game.

title: The Brahmin Nearly Delayed an Indian Release
description: Fallout 3's release in India was reportedly held up over concerns that the two-headed cow-like Brahmin creatures could be seen as offensive given the sacred status of cows in Hinduism.

title: Coulson's Death Nearly Got the Movie an R Rating
description: Marvel actually had to go back to the MPAA three times to lock in a PG-13. The sticking point was Coulson's death - the first cut had Loki's staff bursting clean through his chest, which was way too gory. Whedon dialled it right back to just a stab sound effect and Thor's reaction selling the horror of it, and honestly it hits harder for being left to your imagination.

title: The Title Card Doesn't Show Up Until 12 Minutes In
description: You don't actually see the 'Marvel's The Avengers' title screen until roughly twelve minutes into the film, well after Loki's already caused chaos at the SHIELD facility. Small detail, but it lands as a proper 'this is it' moment - four years of setup movies finally paying off in one title card.

title: First Marvel Film to Cross $1 Billion
description: This was the movie that proved the whole 'shared universe' gamble had actually paid off. It became the first Marvel Studios release to break the billion dollar mark, overtaking The Dark Knight's record in the process and becoming the highest grossing comic book movie ever made at the time.

title: Mark Ruffalo Played Both Banner and the Hulk
description: Thanks to how far motion capture had come by 2012, Ruffalo wasn't just voicing the Hulk in cutaways, he actually performed the majority of Hulk's physical movement himself in a mocap suit. It's the first time in a live action film that both sides of Banner were played by the same actor, and you can genuinely see Ruffalo's mannerisms in the big guy if you look closely.

title: Chris Evans Hated the Cap Helmet
description: Evans was never a fan of his Captain America costume in this one, particularly the helmet, since it had no chin strap and kept sliding around his head between takes. It became enough of a running joke that later MCU movies actually poke fun at the costume whenever the events of this film get brought up.

title: Jeremy Renner Tried to Get Hawkeye Killed Off
description: Renner wasn't happy that Hawkeye spent most of the film brainwashed by Loki instead of doing much actual archery. He was so frustrated with the lack of character work that he reportedly tried to have Barton killed off just to be done with it. He's since said he's glad it didn't happen, given how much more the character got to do in later films.

title: Why Captain America Skips the Shawarma
description: Watch the post credits scene closely and Chris Evans is the only Avenger not eating, and he's clearly holding his hand up against his jaw the whole time. That's because he'd already started filming Snowpiercer and refused to shave his beard, so the makeup team stuck him in a wig and a prosthetic chin and hoped nobody noticed the awkward hand placement covering the seams.

title: Hulk's CGI Body Wasn't Actually Ruffalo's
description: While Ruffalo's face got mapped onto the character, his build didn't quite match the Hulk's proportions. The CGI team based the physique on bodybuilder Steve Romm instead, then layered Ruffalo's facial performance and expressions on top of that frame.

title: The Shawarma Scene Wasn't in the Script
description: That whole silent shawarma scene almost didn't exist. It wasn't in the original screenplay at all - the cast and crew shot it the day after the film's global premiere once Whedon decided the joke from earlier in the film deserved a payoff, and now it's basically the blueprint every MCU post credits scene since has tried to live up to.

title: Robert Downey Jr.'s Snack Stash
description: Downey Jr apparently kept snacks hidden all over the lab set so he'd never go hungry between takes. In one scene where he offers Chris Evans some blueberries, that wasn't scripted at all, it was just Downey munching on his stash and deciding to share, and Whedon liked the moment enough to leave it in the final cut.

title: Black Widow's Russian Interrogation Was Personal for Whedon
description: The opening interrogation scene where Natasha's chatting away in Russian before flipping the situation on her captors was a bit of a passion project moment for Whedon. He studied Russian language and literature back in college, and this was the first time in his career he actually got to put that degree to use on screen.

title: Iron Man's Dented Faceplate After the Thor Headbutt
description: During the forest scrap between Thor and Iron Man, the two trade headbutts, and if you catch Stark flying backward and facing the camera afterward you can see a proper dent left in his faceplate from Thor's skull. Small detail that sells just how much force a god actually hits with.

title: The Nuke Countdown Runs in Real Time
description: A lot of action movies fudge their countdown clocks to stretch out tension, but the nuke timer in the final battle actually tracks pretty closely to the real runtime of that section of the film. It's a tiny bit of restraint that a lot of viewers never clock because they're too busy watching Stark fly it through the portal.

title: Tony Stark's Black Sabbath Shirt
description: Keep an eye on Tony's wardrobe in a few scenes and you'll spot him wearing a Black Sabbath shirt. It's a cheeky little nod to the band's 1970 song 'Iron Man', which is basically the unofficial theme song for the character at this point even though the lyrics have nothing to do with Stark himself.

title: The Galaga High Score Gag
description: Stark clocks a SHIELD agent slacking off playing Galaga on the Helicarrier and makes fun of him for it. The joke doesn't stop there though - the second Tony walks off, the agent goes right back to playing, and if you pause on the screen his score matches the game's existing high score. He was mid-run on the best game of his life and Stark just had to go and ruin it.

title: 'Stuttgart' Was Actually Filmed in Cleveland
description: The scene where Loki forces a crowd to kneel in Germany wasn't shot anywhere near Stuttgart. It was filmed at Tower City Complex on Public Square in Cleveland, Ohio, dressed up to look European for the day.

title: The Opening Facility Sets Up Captain Marvel Years Later
description: The film opens inside the Joint Dark Energy Mission Facility, a SHIELD and NASA site studying the Tesseract as part of Project P.E.G.A.S.U.S. It seems like throwaway setup at the time, but that exact facility becomes central to Captain Marvel years later, when a young Nick Fury and Carol Danvers head there to dig into Dr Wendy Lawson's research.

title: Odin's Ravens Watch Thor and Loki on the Cliff
description: When Thor confronts Loki up on the cliffside, two ravens can be seen scattering as the Asgardians land. They're a nod to Huginn and Muninn, Odin's ravens from Norse mythology and the comics, who fly across the world gathering information and reporting back to him - basically Odin's own surveillance system keeping tabs on his sons.

title: Thanos's 'Court Death' Line Is a Comics Pun
description: In the post credits scene, an alien warns Thanos that attacking Earth would be to 'court death.' It sounds like a throwaway warning, but comic readers clocked it as a deliberate pun straight away, since Thanos is famously, literally in love with the physical embodiment of Death in the source material.

title: Life Model Decoys Are a Deep Comics Cut
description: When Fury mentions Life Model Decoys to explain away Coulson's supposed 'death', it flew right over most audiences' heads back in 2012. It's actually a proper deep cut reference to the comics, where LMDs are robotic doubles built to stand in for real people - Whedon dropped it in years before it would matter to anyone paying attention.

title: Whedon's Early Drafts Had Ant-Man and Wasp Instead
description: Whedon's first pass at the script actually featured Ant-Man and the Wasp, the original founding Avengers in the comics, rather than Hawkeye and Black Widow. He'd even wanted Zooey Deschanel to play the Wasp, but the plan got swapped out in favour of characters Marvel already had set up on screen.

title: Downey Jr Wanted Tony to Open the Film
description: When Downey Jr first read the script he pushed hard for Tony to lead the opening sequence, telling Whedon 'I need to be in the opening sequence, Tony needs to drive this thing.' They actually tried filming it that way, but Downey himself admitted it didn't work, saying everyone else just ended up feeling like 'an arm of the octopus' around him.

title: Thanos Was Whedon's Idea, Not Marvel's
description: The idea of a bigger villain pulling strings behind Loki actually came from Whedon himself. He suggested the Mad Titan Thanos as that hidden mastermind, got him written into the post credits scene, and had no idea at the time just how central that character would become to the entire franchise years later.

title: 'Puny God' Is a Twist on an Old Hulk Line
description: Hulk's iconic put down of Loki wasn't invented for the film. In the comics the Hulk's usual go-to insult is 'puny humans', so swapping it to 'puny god' for a literal god was a small tweak that turned into one of the most quoted lines in the entire MCU.

title: Downey Jr Ad-Libbed Several Iconic Lines
description: Whedon wrote a tight script overall but gave his cast room to improvise, and Downey Jr made the most of it. Lines like his dig at Thor, 'Doth mother know you wear-eth her drapes?', along with his closing 'let's just not come in tomorrow' at the end of the film, weren't in the original screenplay at all.

title: Ruffalo Felt Insecure Stepping Into the Role
description: Taking over Bruce Banner from Edward Norton wasn't easy for Ruffalo, and he apparently spent the first few weeks of filming feeling seriously insecure about it. Both Whedon and Downey Jr had to keep reassuring him he was the right fit, with Ruffalo later saying Norton had essentially 'bequeathed' the part to him.

title: The Neck That Finally Turns
description: Christian Bale spent two movies complaining that the Batsuit's neck piece didn't let him turn his head, so for this one the costume team finally built in an articulated neck. There's even a little in-joke moment where Lucius Fox tells Bruce the new suit lets him 'turn his head' - a wink at exactly that gripe.

title: Joker's Bare Fingers
description: Look closely during the hospital scene with Harvey Dent and you'll notice the Joker isn't wearing his gloves for once, and there's makeup smeared on his fingers. Heath Ledger came up with that detail himself, on the idea that the Joker applies his own face paint and would naturally get some on his hands.

title: Alfred's War Story Wasn't in the Script
description: Michael Caine has said in later interviews that the whole idea of Alfred having a military past came from him, not Nolan's script. That backstory is what gives weight to the 'some men just want to watch the world burn' speech he gives Bruce partway through the film.

title: Gotham's Illinois Plates
description: The fictional Gotham license plates dotted around the film were deliberately designed to look almost identical to real Illinois plates. It meant that whenever an actual Illinois-plated car slipped into a shot by accident, nobody in the audience would notice the difference.

title: A Superhero Movie Shot for IMAX Screens
description: Nolan had wanted to shoot on IMAX cameras for years, and this was his chance - The Dark Knight became the first non-documentary feature ever filmed with them. Only a handful of sequences got the full IMAX treatment, but it set the template for how he'd shoot every Batman film after.

title: Crossing the Billion-Dollar Line
description: This was the very first comic book movie to cross a billion dollars worldwide, a milestone that feels almost routine for superhero films now but was completely unheard of back in 2008.

title: The Bus That Had to Be Rebuilt Mid-Building
description: That bus smashing backwards into the bank during the opening heist looked simple on screen but was a nightmare to actually pull off. The crew had to strip the bus down, reassemble it inside a disused post office behind a hidden false wall, then fire it backwards with an air cannon.

title: Chicago Thought There Was a Real Police Chase
description: While the crew filmed the chase sequence along Lake Street, actual Chicago residents started phoning the police, convinced they were watching a genuine pursuit involving a mystery dark vehicle tearing through the streets.

title: The IMAX Guy Gets His Close-Up
description: Wayne Baker, the technician and consultant who helped run the IMAX cameras on set, sneaks in a brief cameo of his own. It's the only shot in the entire film that's a genuine close-up captured in the IMAX format, a nice bit of behind-the-scenes recognition tucked into the finished movie.

title: The Joker Almost Had a Very Different Face
description: Before Heath Ledger locked the role down in mid-2006, the studio floated names like Paul Bettany, Adrien Brody, Steve Carell and even Robin Williams for the Joker. It's strange to picture now given how completely Ledger's version has come to define the character.

title: Harvey Dent Nearly Went to Someone Else
description: Aaron Eckhart wasn't a lock for Harvey Dent - Liev Schreiber, Josh Lucas and Ryan Phillippe had all shown interest, and Mark Ruffalo actually auditioned for the part. Nolan ended up going with Eckhart after being impressed by his performance in Thank You for Smoking.

title: Rachel Dawes Was a Revolving Door
description: When Katie Holmes decided not to return for the sequel, the studio considered Sarah Michelle Gellar, Isla Fisher, Emily Blunt and Rachel McAdams before Maggie Gyllenhaal ended up taking over the role of Rachel Dawes.

title: The Fake Title Was a Family Nod
description: During production the crew used the working title Rory's First Kiss to throw people off the scent. It wasn't a random phrase - Rory is the name of Christopher Nolan's son.

title: No 'Batman' in the Title
description: For all its box office dominance, this is actually the first Batman feature film where the word 'Batman' doesn't appear anywhere in the title itself.

title: A Theme You Only Hear Twice
description: Composers Hans Zimmer and James Newton Howard made a conscious choice to use Batman's heroic musical theme only twice across the whole film. Their reasoning was that a hummable heroic tune would undercut the darker, messier version of the character they were going for, so hearing it sparingly turns it into what Zimmer called a kind of musical foreshadowing.

title: Biggest Opening Weekend Ever, At the Time
description: The film pulled in over $158 million in its opening weekend, breaking the record that Spider-Man 3 had only just set the previous summer.

title: Ledger Locked Himself Away for a Month
description: To find the Joker, Heath Ledger holed up alone in a hotel room and then his own apartment for roughly a month before filming began. He later described it to Empire as reading every relevant comic he could find, then just sitting and meditating on the character until a voice and a laugh started to emerge.

title: The Joker's Notebook Had a Clockwork Orange Obsession
description: Ledger kept a small diary while getting into character, and one figure kept turning up throughout its pages: Alex DeLarge, Malcolm McDowell's character from A Clockwork Orange. He even practiced replicating McDowell's unnerving 'Kubrick stare' as part of building the Joker's presence.

title: A Hyena Photo Behind the Joker's Laugh
description: Among the clippings and photos in Ledger's preparation diary was an image of a hyena, which people who've seen the documentary footage believe was one of the inspirations behind the Joker's cackling, unhinged laugh in the finished film.

title: Punk Rock Was Part of the Recipe
description: Alongside the comic books and A Clockwork Orange stills, reports on Ledger's preparation say he also drew on the chaotic energy of the Sex Pistols while building his version of the character.

title: That Pencil Really Was on the Table
description: The Joker's 'now you see it, now you don't' pencil gag looks like an obvious CGI trick, but it wasn't one. Visual effects supervisor Nick Davis said the team avoided building a digital pencil because the film was shot in IMAX, and a CG element would never blend seamlessly into an image that huge and detailed.

title: One Scene, Two Separate Takes, Zero CGI
description: The pencil disappearing trick was actually filmed twice: once with the pencil standing up in the table, and once with the stuntman slamming his head onto the exact same spot with nothing there at all. The two shots were then cut together in the edit to create the illusion.

title: Knocked Out Three Times for One Scene
description: Stuntman Charles Jarman took a real beating filming the pencil scene, getting genuinely knocked unconscious three separate times across roughly 22 takes over two days. In one of the takes Heath Ledger actually broke character mid-scene to check if Jarman was okay before slipping straight back into the Joker.

title: Ledger Stayed in Character Off-Camera Too
description: According to Jarman, Ledger would leave the room between takes on the pencil scene and only ever return to set already back in character as the Joker, never breaking it in front of the crew except that one moment he checked on his stunt partner.

title: Hurricane Shutdown
entertainment: Pirates of the Caribbean: Dead Man's Chest
description: Filming wasn't smooth sailing the whole way through. Hurricane Wilma barrelled toward the shoot while the crew was working in the islands, and everyone had to pack up and evacuate all the way back to Los Angeles until it was safe to return.

title: Elizabeth's Hair Wasn't Really Hers
entertainment: Pirates of the Caribbean: Dead Man's Chest
description: Keira Knightley had chopped her hair into a short pixie cut for the film Domino, and there simply wasn't time to grow it back before shooting started. So most of Elizabeth Swann's flowing locks in this one are actually extensions.

title: No Ghosts Allowed
entertainment: Pirates of the Caribbean: Dead Man's Chest
description: Early plans had the Flying Dutchman crewed by literal ghosts, but director Gore Verbinski wasn't keen on that idea. Instead they went with living, barnacle-encrusted crewmen, brought to life using motion capture suits on real actors.

title: Tim Burton's Secret Hand
entertainment: Pirates of the Caribbean: Dead Man's Chest
description: Johnny Depp's other favourite director popped up in an unexpected way here. Tim Burton, busy with his own projects at the time, still carved out time to help design the look of Davy Jones' grotesque crew.

title: The Kraken Learned From a Kaiju
entertainment: Pirates of the Caribbean: Dead Man's Chest
description: Getting the Kraken's tentacles to move convincingly was a nightmare for the animators. The solution came from an unlikely place: the animation director had his team study the octopus fight scene from the 1962 classic King Kong vs. Godzilla for inspiration.

title: Davy Jones' Coffee Cup Face
entertainment: Pirates of the Caribbean: Dead Man's Chest
description: Bill Nighy's iconic tentacled face didn't come from squids or barnacles as a reference. The grimy texture and colouring were actually developed from a scanned image of a dirty, discarded Styrofoam coffee cup.

title: That Kraken Spit Was Real
entertainment: Pirates of the Caribbean: Dead Man's Chest
description: Not everything in that climactic Kraken confrontation was digital. When the beast spits and sends Jack flying, that gunk hitting Johnny Depp was genuine practical slime, not a CGI effect.

title: Island Hopping for Real
entertainment: Pirates of the Caribbean: Dead Man's Chest
description: The first film stuck to a single Caribbean island for its shoot. This sequel had a much bigger budget and went for it, filming across Palos Verdes, the Bahamas, Dominica, and St. Vincent, plus sets built at the Disney studio lot.

title: Two Sequels, One Shoot
entertainment: Pirates of the Caribbean: Dead Man's Chest
Pirates of the Caribbean: At World's End
description: To save money and keep everything consistent, Dead Man's Chest was filmed back-to-back with its follow-up, At World's End. It made for a brutal, marathon production schedule across multiple countries, but it let Disney release both only a year apart.

title: They Built Actual Working Ships
entertainment: Pirates of the Caribbean: Dead Man's Chest
description: Rather than relying purely on models and green screen, the production built two full-scale, functioning ships for the film: real-life versions of the Black Pearl and the Flying Dutchman that could genuinely sail.

title: Banned Over the Cannibal Scene
entertainment: Pirates of the Caribbean: Dead Man's Chest
description: The film's stop on the cannibal island wasn't just unsettling for some audiences, it got the movie banned outright in China, where censors objected specifically to the cannibalism content.

title: Genuinely Shocked by Barbossa
entertainment: Pirates of the Caribbean: Dead Man's Chest
description: The cast's stunned reactions in the film's final scene weren't acted. Everyone had been told that Zoe Saldaña's Anamaria was the one who'd walk out at the end, so their surprise at seeing Geoffrey Rush's Barbossa instead was completely real.

title: Keira's Own Idea
entertainment: Pirates of the Caribbean: Dead Man's Chest
description: The moment where Elizabeth kisses Jack and then handcuffs him to the ship wasn't dreamed up by the writers. Keira Knightley herself pitched the idea for that scene.

title: An Accent Coached From Home
entertainment: Pirates of the Caribbean: Dead Man's Chest
description: Tia Dalma speaks with a partial Jamaican accent, and that's no coincidence. Naomie Harris's own mother is Jamaican and worked as her dialect coach to help her nail the sound during production.

title: The Jar of Dirt Was Unscripted
entertainment: Pirates of the Caribbean: Dead Man's Chest
description: Jack Sparrow's now-famous line about having a jar of dirt wasn't in the script at all. Johnny Depp ad-libbed it on the spot, and the confused, amused reactions from the rest of the crew on camera are completely genuine.

title: Davy Jones Almost Looked Very Different
entertainment: Pirates of the Caribbean: Dead Man's Chest
description: Bill Nighy wasn't the first name attached to Davy Jones. Richard E. Grant, Christopher Walken, Jim Broadbent, and Iain Glen were all in the conversation for the role before Nighy was eventually cast.

title: Keith Richards Missed His Cue
entertainment: Pirates of the Caribbean: Dead Man's Chest
Pirates of the Caribbean: At World's End
description: Keith Richards was originally supposed to make a cameo in this film, but touring commitments got in the way and he had to bow out. He'd eventually show up as Jack Sparrow's father a couple of sequels later instead.

title: Anamaria Never Came Back
entertainment: Pirates of the Caribbean: Dead Man's Chest
description: Anamaria was actually written back into the script for this film, but Zoe Saldaña turned it down. She's said her time on the first movie was rough enough that it nearly put her off acting altogether, and she decided it wasn't worth returning for.

title: Pirates in Your Happy Meal
entertainment: Pirates of the Caribbean: Dead Man's Chest
description: The film got the full fast-food tie-in treatment, with McDonald's releasing a set of eight Happy Meal toys based on it, plus another set a couple of years later blending in elements from the theme park ride too.

title: Accents That Don't Match the Actors
entertainment: Pirates of the Caribbean: Dead Man's Chest
description: There's a fun bit of casting irony hiding in the film. Swedish actor Stellan Skarsgård plays the very English Bootstrap Bill Turner, while English actor Bill Nighy plays the distinctly Scottish-sounding Davy Jones.

title: Written on the Fly
entertainment: Pirates of the Caribbean: Dead Man's Chest
description: The script was nowhere near finished when cameras started rolling. Storyboards had to be drawn up without a completed screenplay, and the writers ended up on set writing scenes while filming was actually happening around them.

title: Third Film Ever to Cross $1 Billion
entertainment: Pirates of the Caribbean: Dead Man's Chest
description: This was only the third movie in history to hit the billion-dollar mark worldwide, following Titanic and The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King, and it got there faster than either of them had managed.

title: Biggest Opening Weekend of All Time
entertainment: Pirates of the Caribbean: Dead Man's Chest
description: When it launched, this sequel didn't just do well, it smashed the all-time opening weekend record, easily outpacing the previous record holder and pulling in nearly three times what the first Pirates film made on its own debut weekend.

title: That Wheel Fight Photo Isn't From This Movie
entertainment: Pirates of the Caribbean: Dead Man's Chest
description: A lot of people picture Jack Sparrow himself duelling atop the giant rolling wheel, but in the actual film it's Will and Norrington fighting up there while Jack just gets tossed around inside it. The image everyone remembers of Jack on top of the wheel is actually from the parody film Epic Movie, not this one at all.

title: A Heart Locked Away From Love
entertainment: Pirates of the Caribbean: Dead Man's Chest
description: Within the story, Davy Jones wasn't always a monster. He was once a man who fell in love, and unable to bear the pain that came with it, he cut out his own beating heart and locked it inside the chest that gives the film its name.

title: Rank Is Written on Their Skin
entertainment: Pirates of the Caribbean: Dead Man's Chest
description: There's an intentional bit of world-building buried in the Flying Dutchman's crew designs. The more twisted and creature-like a crew member looks, the higher up the ship's hierarchy they actually are, so the most monstrous faces belong to the ones closest to Davy Jones.

title: Charles Martinet's Arcade Cameo
description: The actual voice of video game Mario, Charles Martinet, shows up in the movie itself. He plays a character called Giuseppe who's hunched over an arcade cabinet playing a game called 'Jump Man', which is a cheeky nod to Mario's original name from the 1981 Donkey Kong arcade game.

title: Martinet's Second Role
description: Not content with one cameo, Charles Martinet also voices Mario and Luigi's dad in the film. It's a much more disguised performance than his Giuseppe cameo, so most people miss it completely on their first watch.

title: Foreman Spike's Grudge
description: Mario and Luigi's old boss Spike isn't just a random side character, he's pulled straight from Wrecking Crew, a fairly obscure 1985 Famicom title. In the movie he gets a dig in at Mario, calling him a joke, clearly still bitter about being his old employer.

title: World 1-1 Comes To Brooklyn
description: Before the brothers get sucked into the warp pipe, they sprint across a Brooklyn construction site to make it to a job on time. Look at the layout closely and it's basically a live-action recreation of World 1-1 from the original Super Mario Bros, right down to Mario sliding down a sign post like it's the end-of-level flagpole.

title: Mario's GameCube Ringtone
description: Keep your ears open during the plumbing commercial scene, because when Mario's phone goes off, the ringtone is the Nintendo GameCube startup chime. It's a blink-and-you'll-miss-it audio gag that only really lands if you grew up with the console.

title: Punch-Out Pizzeria
description: Mario and Luigi watch their own cringey ad back in a place called Punch-Out Pizzeria, complete with newspaper clippings of Little Mac's boxing exploits pinned up on the walls. It's a nice little shoutout to Nintendo's Punch-Out!! series tucked into an otherwise unremarkable diner scene.

title: A Restaurant Called Duck Hunt
description: As the brothers walk home through Brooklyn, they pass a restaurant with the French name Chasse au Canard painted on the window. Translate it and you get Duck Hunt, a sly little tribute to the 1985 NES light gun classic hiding in plain sight.

title: Mario's Bedroom Wall Posters
description: Mario and Luigi's bedroom is basically a shrine to Nintendo history if you pause and look properly. There's an F-Zero poster showing off Captain Falcon's ride, plus a poster of the sunglasses-wearing polar bear from the Ice Climber games, both easy to miss while the scene is moving.

title: Down to Level 1-2
description: When the brothers head into Brooklyn's sewers to fix a burst pipe, the music playing underneath is a callback to World 1-2 from the original Super Mario Bros, the very first underground level in the series. There's even a sign behind Luigi labelling the area Level 1-2, just to make sure nobody missed it.

title: Pauline's Blink-And-You'll-Miss-It Cameo
description: Long before Peach, Mario's very first damsel to rescue in 1981's Donkey Kong was a woman named Pauline. She gets a quick, easy to overlook cameo in the movie, a nod to fans who remember her as the original Mario girl before she got sidelined for decades.
